q1-capability.title: What capability changes, in present tense?
q1-capability.imperative: State the capability delta behaviorally. Resolve from the issue text + code: this is a hardening/refactor, so name what the system will DO afterwards that it does not do now, and what must stay byte-identical. Record code evidence.
q1-capability.finding: FACT (code evidence). CAPABILITY DELTA: the DriverFingerprint store REFUSES a structurally ill-formed cell identity at its own boundary, instead of accepting five loose strings and only discovering the problem (or not) at row-write time. Today store.py:193 write_fingerprint(driver,era,vocabulary,channel,what_measure,observations) and store.py:255 get_fingerprint(driver,era,vocabulary,channel,what_measure) / store.py:298 row_count(same) take four bare str plus a ClassVocabulary; the only identity validation is the era-vs-vocabulary.rules_era equality check (store.py:163) and the reserved-what_measure refusal (store.py:213). The six-field validation that address.py:88 __post_init__ performs (non-empty str, no CELL_KEY_DELIMITER, known what_measure) is reached only AFTER the write path has already committed to a row set (address constructed at store.py:233, inside the per-class loop). Afterwards, that validation happens at the CALL, before any store work. MUST STAY IDENTICAL: the four keystone store invariants named in store.py:10-32 -- non-NULL cell_key, k-cells-always-populated, loud refusal with no silent substitution, and NO fit-on-read -- plus every fitted number fit.py produces. This is a type/seam refactor: zero change to any mean, sigma, support_n, status, or coverage verdict. H2 and H3 are separate, non-interacting hygiene items with no runtime coupling to H1.

q2-address-shape.title: Can the store API literally be typed on CellAddress?
q2-address-shape.imperative: Compare CellAddress's six fields against the store methods' actual key. Resolve from src/physics/fingerprint/address.py and store.py. If they do not match, say exactly how, because that misfit governs H1's whole shape.
q2-address-shape.finding: FACT -- NO, and this is the finding that governs H1's whole shape. CellAddress (address.py:62-86) has SIX fields: driver, era, vocabulary_version, class_id, channel, what_measure. The store's methods key on FIVE arguments, and the mapping is NOT one-to-one: (a) class_id is ABSENT from the store's key -- it is the fan-out axis. store.py:225 loops class_id over vocabulary.class_ids and constructs one CellAddress per class inside the loop (store.py:233); get_fingerprint does the mirror-image loop at store.py:275. Every call handles exactly vocabulary.k cells, never one. (b) vocabulary_version is not passed as a string at all -- it is READ OFF the ClassVocabulary argument as vocabulary.vocabulary_id (store.py:234, :270, :310). So a literal 'store API typed on CellAddress' is unattainable: CellAddress addresses ONE cell and mandates a non-empty class_id (address.py:88-94), while the store's unit of work is the k-cell GROUP. Passing a CellAddress whose class_id is a sentinel would be a lie against the value object's own documented invariant. The genuine H1 target is therefore the address PREFIX -- the tuple that is constant across a call. Note store.py's own docstring already names that tuple: 'a write targets a (driver, era, channel, what_measure) SLOT' (store.py:22-23, echoed at store.py:186 and :301). That is existing in-repo prose for exactly this object, so the run inherits a name rather than coining one.

q3-slot-design.title: Given the misfit, what value object does the store API take?
q3-slot-design.imperative: A choice the principal owns: the issue says 'typed on CellAddress' but the store keys a k-cell GROUP, not a cell. Present the candidate shapes with a recommendation. No human is reachable this engagement, so record the question as it would have been asked, rule it, and state the authority.
q3-slot-design.finding: DECISION -- no human reachable; question recorded, ruled by the Commander under the engagement's self-decide instruction. WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'Issue #698 H1 says type the store on CellAddress, but CellAddress addresses one cell and the store addresses a k-cell group (q2). Three shapes: (A) a new frozen value object carrying the four constant identity strings (driver, era, channel, what_measure), with ClassVocabulary still supplying vocabulary_version + class_ids, and the object as the SOLE constructor of CellAddress; (B) the same but ALSO carrying vocabulary_version, requiring a second refusal path when it disagrees with the passed vocabulary; (C) rewrite the store as a per-cell API taking a real CellAddress, moving the k-fan-out to callers. I recommend A. Accept?' RULING: (A). Named FingerprintSlot, defined in address.py beside CellAddress (one file, one identity space), with a slot.address_for(class_id, vocabulary) -> CellAddress method that becomes the only way a CellAddress is built on the store path. REASONS. (C) is rejected outright: the k-cells-always-populated and NO-fit-on-read invariants (store.py:14-32) are #666 Protected Intent and live precisely IN the fan-out; moving it to callers destroys them and is far outside a hardening issue. (B) is rejected because vocabulary_version would then be asserted twice per call -- once on the slot, once via vocabulary.vocabulary_id -- which buys no safety (ClassVocabulary is a required argument regardless, for class_ids and require_fittable) and costs a second EraVocabularyMismatchError-class refusal path plus its tests. (A) validates exactly the four arguments that are genuinely loose strings today and leaves the already-typed ClassVocabulary as the vocabulary_version authority, matching the existing single-source pattern. NAME: FingerprintSlot is not coined dialect -- store.py:22-23/:186/:301 already calls this exact tuple a 'slot' in prose. AUTHORITY: Commander, engagement instruction 'record what you would have asked, decide it yourself'. GRADE: @grade: settled/inherited -- the k-cell-group shape follows from #666's Protected Intent, not from this run's preference; the NAME alone is @grade: guess (a human may rename with no structural consequence).

q4-blast-radius.imperative: Enumerate every caller of write_fingerprint/get_fingerprint/row_count in src/, scripts/, and tests/. Explicitly check the architecture map's claim that instrument_panel reads store.get_fingerprint directly -- verify against source rather than trusting the packet prose.
q4-blast-radius.finding: FACT -- caller set closed by grep over src/ scripts/ tests/. PRODUCTION src (2 files, 3 call sites): src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:356 store.write_fingerprint(driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure, observations, allow_unverified=...) -- the SOLE writer anywhere; src/physics/pilot/pipeline.py:257 (run_stage_g) and :325 (run_stage_h) store.get_fingerprint(driver, vocabulary.rules_era, vocabulary, channel, DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE). SCRIPTS (2): scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:124 get_fingerprint; scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py:173 get_fingerprint. TESTS (3 files): tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_store.py (~20 sites incl. row_count at :111/:125 and the three refusal tests at :132/:140/:153-161), test_fit.py:160 get_fingerprint, test_bounded_validation.py:173/:267 get_fingerprint + :326/:333 row_count. MAP CLAIM CHECKED AND CORRECTED: docs/architecture/packets/physics.md:2753 says instrument_panel 'Reads UN-AGGREGATED fingerprint.store.get_fingerprint cells directly'. Verified against source -- FALSE as an import/call claim: neither src/physics/instrument_panel/*.py nor scripts/instrument_panel_668_report.py references DriverFingerprintStore or get_fingerprint at all (the only fingerprint import is FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS at replication.py:61). The panel RECEIVES already-fetched cell objects; the pilot is the fetcher. The packet's prose is about un-aggregated-cells-rather-than-the-#667-join, not about who calls the store -- but read literally it would have sent an implementer hunting a non-existent call site. Consequence: instrument_panel needs NO change under H1, and the packet wording is a triage candidate. Also confirmed src/physics/fingerprint/__init__.py (8L) re-exports nothing -- no change there. This corroborates lesson:verify-subagent-self-report-not-just-green-check and lesson:cartographer-audit-gaps: check_arch_map.py is green over this exact prose.

q5-tightening-scope.title: How much input tightening rides along, given 'no behavior change to fit/coverage'?
q5-tightening-scope.imperative: Rule on which validations the new boundary enforces: CellAddress parity only, or also channel-set membership; and confirm the dormant reserved-what_measure slot stays CONSTRUCTIBLE-but-refused-at-write. Record what would have been asked, rule it, state the authority.
q5-tightening-scope.finding: DECISION -- no human reachable; recorded and ruled by the Commander. WOULD HAVE ASKED: 'FingerprintSlot construction will reject inputs the store accepts today. Exact CellAddress parity (non-empty str, no pipe delimiter, what_measure in the known set) -- or also channel membership in FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS, which CellAddress does NOT enforce? The latter is a real behavior tightening beyond parity.' RULING, three parts. (1) EXACT CellAddress PARITY, nothing more. FingerprintSlot reuses the same per-field validator address.py:88-99 applies, so validation is literally shared code, not a re-implementation that can drift. (2) NO channel-set membership check. address.py:35 defines FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS but CellAddress never enforces it, so enforcing it on the slot would put the two objects out of parity and change refusal behavior for a channel string neither object rejects today; fit.py:347-350 already validates channel against its own _VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL on the write path. Enforcing the channel set is a separate decision with its own blast radius (it would hard-wire the constant against a future third channel) -> TRIAGE CANDIDATE, not this run. (3) The dormant reserved what_measure slot MUST stay CONSTRUCTIBLE-but-refused-at-write. This is the single highest-risk regression in H1: address.py:16-19 and :40-42 document epic #659 ruling 4 (present-but-unused slots), address.py:100-104 ACCEPTS a RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES value at construction, and store.py:213-217 raises ReservedWhatMeasureError only at write. If FingerprintSlot rejected reserved measures at construction it would both break the documented ruling and flip the error type that tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_store.py:153-161 asserts. An unknown measure like 'banana' DOES newly raise ValueError at slot construction where the store previously wrote rows for it -- that is exactly the acceptance H1 asks for ('an ill-formed address can't reach the store'), no current caller does it, and it gets an explicit test. Also preserved: slot construction stays VOCABULARY-BLIND, so era-vs-vocabulary.rules_era disagreement still surfaces as EraVocabularyMismatchError from store.py:163 and not as a construction ValueError -- test_store.py:132/:140 pass a valid-but-wrong era string and must keep getting the same exception. AUTHORITY: Commander, engagement self-decide instruction. @grade: settled/inherited (parts 1 and 3 follow from #666's recorded ruling 4 and the existing tests); part 2's deferral @grade: guess -- settle: a one-line grep showing whether any caller ever passes a channel outside FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS.

q6-h2-scope.title: Is fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py the only script missing the sys.path guard?
q6-h2-scope.imperative: Check the whole #666/#667/#668/#675 script family for the worktree-first sys.path guard and record which have it, so H2's one-file scope is either confirmed or corrected. Record the canonical guard form from the reference script.
q6-h2-scope.finding: FACT -- H2's one-file scope CONFIRMED exactly. Swept the whole epic-659 fingerprint script family for the guard: scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py HAS it (lines 28-29), scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py HAS it (lines 42-43), scripts/instrument_panel_668_report.py HAS it (line 45, via an aliased _sys import). scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py does NOT: its import block runs lines 86-100 with no sys.path touch anywhere in the file, yet line 99 does 'from src.physics.fingerprint.frozen_constants import FINGERPRINT_FROZEN' and lines 98/100 reach src.common and src.physics.layer2. So the one script the issue names is the one and only gap -- no scope correction needed, and no sibling sweep to plan. CANONICAL GUARD FORM, quoted from the reference the issue cites (scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:71-75): a comment explaining that direct-file invocation puts only scripts/ on sys.path, then _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / if str(_REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path: / sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT)). Note .parent.parent is the in-repo idiom; the issue text writes parents[1], which is equivalent -- follow the repo idiom for consistency with the three sibling scripts. The guard must be placed AFTER 'from __future__ import annotations' (line 86) and BEFORE the first src.* import (line 98), which requires moving 'import sys' and the existing 'from pathlib import Path' (line 92) above it. This is the editable-install .pth trap already banked in project memory: pytest inserts its own root so the test suite never sees it, which is why it survived #666 review.

q7-h3-truth.title: Is H3's premise true -- are these artifacts already ignored via .agent-work/?
q7-h3-truth.imperative: Test the issue's stated premise against .gitignore and git ls-files. Determine what a bare non-epic run of the fingerprint family actually drops on disk and whether each lands in a tracked path. Do not assume the issue's premise is correct.
q7-h3-truth.finding: FACT -- the issue's PREMISE IS FALSE, and correcting it changes what H3 should actually do. #698 H3 says the JSONs are 'already ignored via .agent-work/'. They are not: .gitignore contains NO '.agent-work/' rule. It ignores only narrow sub-patterns under it (.agent-work/**/*.pkl, *.npz, *.db, scratch/, ckpt/, backtests/, plus four one-off record dirs). .agent-work/ is a TRACKED tree here by design -- engine-config.json rules_root says 'Commit Commander work logs only after the work package is finished and archived under .agent-work/archive', and git ls-files confirms .agent-work/archive/2026-07-26-666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/coverage_675_verdict.json and .../bounded_fit_summary.json are BOTH tracked today. That is correct behavior for archived run evidence, not a leak. THE REAL EXPOSURE is what a bare re-run drops in the LIVE (non-archive) path. (a) scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py:123 writes VERDICT_PATH = .agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/coverage_675_verdict.json unconditionally -- no --out flag (:472-473 expose only --slice-db and --n-reps), so a re-run outside an epic work area writes a regenerable JSON into an untracked-but-not-ignored path that a git add -A would stage. Same shape for scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:48 (_OUT_PATH bounded_fit_summary.json) and scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py:70. (b) HIGHER-VALUE FINDING, outside the JSON framing the issue used: store.py:50 DEFAULT_DB_PATH = 'data/driver_fingerprint.db', and grep of .gitignore for 'driver_fingerprint' returns NOTHING -- while every sibling own-DB IS ignored (/data/reference_utilization.db #664, /data/segment_maps.db #662, /data/driver_utility_observables.db + /data/driver_utility.db #628). So a default-path fit run creates an untracked binary SQLite DB in data/, exactly the artifact class the archive step's own git-change-policy deny-globs exist to stop. This is the same omission class H3 was written to catch, one notch more consequential than the JSON, and it belongs in this fix.

The real importer set is closed and small (q4): tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/ (all 10 files, which covers store, fit, address, join, vocabulary, bounded-validation and heldout) PLUS tests/unit/physics/test_pilot*.py for the two pilot call sites. Concretely: py -m pytest tests/unit/physics/fingerprint tests/unit/physics -k pilot. Three further rulings. (1) lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests applies with full force -- store.py is a ratified, consumed #666 module, so the gate must re-run its OWN pre-existing test files (test_store.py, test_fit.py, test_bounded_validation.py) unmodified-in-intent, not merely the new malformed-address test. Every existing refusal assertion must still raise the SAME exception type. It must be a bare direct-file invocation from a directory that is not the repo root, proving the import resolves; and the honest version runs it in a worktree, since that is the actual failure the Admiral verify hit. H3's acceptance is git check-ignore returning exit 0 on each newly-ignored path plus exit 1 on a control path, not a test. AUTHORITY: Commander, engagement self-decide instruction. @grade: settled/inherited (the scoping rule is project doctrine plus a banked lesson, not this run's preference).

consolidation.summary: #698 is three independent hardening items over the #666 fingerprint package. H1 is the real work: the DriverFingerprintStore's three methods take four loose identity strings plus a ClassVocabulary, and the six-field CellAddress validation is reached only inside the write loop, after the row set is already committed to. The issue's literal acceptance ('store API typed on CellAddress') is unattainable because CellAddress addresses ONE cell while the store addresses a k-cell GROUP -- class_id is the fan-out axis and vocabulary_version is read off the vocabulary. RULED: introduce a frozen FingerprintSlot(driver, era, channel, what_measure) in address.py, sharing CellAddress's exact validator and exposing address_for(class_id, vocabulary) as the sole CellAddress constructor on the store path; the name is inherited from store.py's own prose, not coined. Tightening is parity-only: no channel-set check (triaged), and the dormant reserved what_measure slot MUST stay constructible-but-refused-at-write or epic #659 ruling 4 and test_store.py:153-161 both break. Blast radius is closed and small: fit.py:356, pilot/pipeline.py:257+:325, two scripts, three test files -- and the architecture packet's claim that instrument_panel reads the store directly is FALSE against source, so the panel needs no change. H2 is confirmed exactly one file: fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py is the only member of its four-script family without the sys.path guard, and pytest is structurally blind to the defect so its acceptance must be a bare direct-file run. H3's premise is FALSE -- .agent-work/ is a tracked tree by project convention, not gitignored -- and the reframed item finds a better target than the issue's JSON framing: store.py:50's default data/driver_fingerprint.db is absent from .gitignore while every sibling own-DB is present. Evidence is scoped to the closed importer set per project doctrine and two banked lessons, never a blanket suite.
